findings.text: switching fence_argv from protected_paths() to declared_protected_paths() silently defeated this file's declared negative-control driver. _negative_control_report monkeypatches _backends.protected_paths with _without_pool to strip Code/.reckon-worktrees, but fence_argv no longer calls protected_paths, so the mutation does not reach the fence. Verified: with protected_paths monkeypatched to the stripped list (pool absent) fence_argv still emits the pool's --ro-bind (True), so the driver now reproduces no red and would report the control as non-reproducing. The file is outside this node's write scope, so this is a follow-on for that file's owner, not a fix here.

the refusal arm is scoped to layer-declared paths only (required=_declared_paths(config, PROTECTED_PATHS_KEY, home)), so a shipped default that stays absent past the bound is left out and the launch proceeds with that path writable. ~/.claude.json is a shipped default (_backends.py:2527), so the plan's own statement that skipping a missing protected source 'would be worse, because the worker would then run with that path writable' still applies to it whenever the plan's wait (0.5s) is exceeded. The manifest and fragment disclose this (a host without ~/.netrc must not lose every launch), which is a defensible trade, but it is a literal gap in the done-when's refusal clause and in 'launches only once every protected path is bound'.

the vanish-after-composition window is unhandled: a protected source that disappears between composition and subprocess.Popen(plan.argv) still aborts the launch with the same bwrap message. dispatch.py is outside this node's four write paths and held by a concurrent node; the manifest records it as a blocker and the fragment as a follow-on, which is the correct disposition.

item_verdicts.call_sites: three call sites listed; the operative change is _backends.py:2923 and :2931 inside fence_argv.
item_verdicts.diff: read 9fe5d8204..6be8e8d3 (3 files, +266/-26): intent/on-disk split of the protected set, bounded shared wait, declared-path refusal, fence_argv rewired.
item_verdicts.done_when: clauses 1,3,4,5,6 hold; clause 2 holds for declared paths and reappearing defaults but not for an absent shipped default.
item_verdicts.goal: mostly achieved: a momentarily absent protected bind source is now waited for, bounded and together, with the bound a named constant, and both required tests exist; the refusal is narrower than the done-when reads, applying to declared paths but not to shipped defaults.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; complete, both suite arms completed EXIT=0, derived added-failure set empty, residual window disclosed.
item_verdicts.write_paths: three files touched, all within the granted write scope; the out-of-scope dispatch.py fix was declined and reported.

justifications.durability: the guarded behaviour is genuinely guarded and not merely green: I re-extracted the reviewed tree to scratch, removed the bounded wait in _await_protected_sources, and the delayed-file test then fails (review-negative-control.log: 1 failed, 2 passed EXIT=1, failing id tests/test_protected_bind_waits_for_its_source.py::test_a_protected_file_that_appears_after_a_delay_is_bound), matching the run's own gate-negative-control.log. Weakness: the delayed-file test is timing-based (a threading.Timer(0.2) against a 10x0.05s=0.5s bound), so it carries a small flake margin under heavy load.
justifications.evidence: receipts are concrete and reconcile with the logs: gate-base.log (revision 9fe5d8204) ends '167 passed' EXIT=0, gate-head.log (revision 926a9dcd) ends '170 passed' EXIT=0, gate-negative-control.log shows the retry-removal red (1 failed, 2 passed EXIT=1), and repro-incident.txt quotes the base defect (declared absent path bound read-only: False; vanish-after-check exit 1 with the bwrap message). I independently re-ran the three new tests at the reviewed head 6be8e8d3 (review-rerun.log: 3 passed EXIT=0) and reproduced the red myself (review-negative-control.log). Weakness: the recorded head arm ran at 926a9dcd, one docs-only commit short of the reviewed head 6be8e8d3; the code under test is identical across the two, so the zero-added-failure conclusion is unaffected.
justifications.fit: the change extends the existing fence idiom rather than inventing a parallel one: the intent-versus-on-disk split is expressed as _named_protected_paths / _declared_protected_paths with declared_protected_paths and protected_paths as thin views, protected_read_only_binds keeps its role and adds a keyword-only required= arm, and fence_argv is the one composition point. Both commits carry a conventional subject and a body; no attribution and no plan, sprint or version identifier appears in code, symbols or comments.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the momentary-absence incident is closed and every test the done-when names exists, but the refusal clause is implemented only for layer-declared paths. ~/.claude.json is a shipped default, so a launch can still proceed with it writable when it stays absent past the 0.5s bound, which the plan named as the worse outcome. The disclosure and the host-without-netrc counterexample make the trade defensible, so this is a partial rather than a miss.
justifications.scope_discipline: exemplary: the diff touches exactly the three granted paths (reckon/_backends.py, tests/test_protected_bind_waits_for_its_source.py, the evidence fragment), and the worker refused to edit reckon/crew/dispatch.py, which it does not own, returning the vanish-before-sandbox-start window as a named blocker and follow_ons instead of expanding scope.
